text:
Hannah: FYI customer reported sudden tail-latency jump for hosted generate endpoints (model rdx-opt-7b) starting ~2026-03-10T11:02Z. p95 went from ~0.3s to ~1.1s for short requests (<64 tokens).

Jorge: saw the alert too. spikes concentrated in us-west pools. any config changes around that UTC window?

Lili: we pushed a kernel selection tweak earlier today (08:40 UTC) that biases toward flash-attention-2 when shapes are eligible. rollout was gradual but hit most pools by ~09:10.

Tomo: quick ask: can infra force a short-term fallback to SDPA on the impacted pools to see if that reverts the regression?

infra-oncall: applying override now -> setting KERNEL_PREFERENCE_OVERRIDE={"prefer":"sdpa","scope":"model:rdx-opt-7b|seq<=48|batch=1"} to targeted pool rdx-hosted-us-west-2-pool-3. hot-reload in progress, ETA ~4m.

Hannah: support needs a minimal repro for the customer and a short write-up of what we changed. could someone paste a curl they used for repro?

Jorge: repro we run in staging (sequential requests, no streaming):

```
# repro_seq.sh
MODEL=rdx-opt-7b
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"'$MODEL'","input":"hey","max_tokens":24,"stream":false}' -w "\\nTOTAL_TIME:%{time_total}\\n"
done
```

Baseline pre-rollout: p95 ~0.28s, p99 ~0.85s. After kernel change: p95 ~0.9s, p99 ~1.6s (batch=1, short seqs).

Lili: logs from a slow request (request-id=rq-77f):

```
[2026-03-10T11:05:12Z] rq=rq-77f model=rdx-opt-7b seq_len=12 batch_size=1 kernel=flash_attn_v2 compile_flags=O3_ATTEN
[2026-03-10T11:05:12Z] attention_path=flash_attn_v2 kv_cache=false latency=1.12s tokens_processed=18
```

Lili: note — larger seq lengths and batched requests didn't show the regression. looks like overhead per-launch dominates for tiny shapes on our card.

Tomo: good catch. flash-attn variants often have high kernel launch / setup cost that is amortized only for larger seqs or larger batch sizes.

infra-oncall: override applied to 100% for the pool; routing should hit SDPA now. monitoring metrics...

ops-bot: metric update -> pool rdx-hosted-us-west-2-pool-3 p95 decreased from 0.92s to 0.33s within 2 minutes of override. p99 trending down too.

Hannah: excellent. Support can reply to customer: temporary kernel override to SDPA applied; asking them to validate. Also include repro script and note we're working on permanent fix.

Jorge: permanent options: 1) refine selector thresholds so flash-attn only for seq>=64 or batch>=4; 2) compile a small-seq-optimized flash-attn micro-kernel variant (flash_attn_smallseq); 3) add CI perf gate to detect regressions on short-seq workloads during kernel rollouts.

Lili: compile path estimated 36-48h (build + smoke + perf canaries). selector tweak is faster and lower risk: we can add rule KERNEL_SELECTOR_RULES="rdx-opt-*/seq<=48->prefer:sdpa" and ship in minutes.

Tomo: also suggest telemetry change: add a lightweight log entry per request (sampling 1%) with fields model, seq_len, batch_size, chosen_kernel so we can quickly correlate future spikes.

infra-oncall: will keep override in place for 24h and add the selector rule as an additional protective layer.

Hannah: Sarah from support asked for the exact mitigation text to send; draft: \"Investigation: recent kernel-selection rollout favored FlashAttention for eligible shapes; this increased per-request latency for short sequences at batch=1 due to kernel launch overhead on our GPUs. Mitigation: we temporarily forced SDPA kernels for affected pools and models (KERNEL_PREFERENCE_OVERRIDE applied). Next steps: refine selector thresholds and build a small-seq optimized kernel.\"

support-bot: Ticket #24217: status=waiting_for_customer. note=Temporary kernel override applied; asking customer to confirm latency is improved.

Jorge: follow-ups assigned: Lili -> build small-seq kernel + perf canary (owner), Tomo -> telemetry sampling change + CI perf test for seq<=48 (owner), infra -> blacklist-free rollout guard (10% canary for 1h + automated rollback on >15% p95 regression).

Hannah: let's keep the internal follow-up ticket open until we have the new kernel or selector change in prod. close customer-facing ticket after they verify improvement.

Lili: recording bench numbers and the override string in runbooks/kernel-rollbacks.md. I'll start the compile branch now (flag: COMPILE_SMALLSEQ=1) and report back in the staging perf channel.

ops-bot: action log -> override applied by infra-oncall, monitoring alerted and confirmed improvement, follow-up tickets created.

Hannah: thanks all. lesson: kernel rollouts need a small-seq perf validation step on our hardware profiles before wide rollout.
